To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

GABAergic neurons mediate the inhibitory component of the vestibulo-ocular reflex in the tadpole superior oblique nucleus, and that the pharmacological profile of inhibitory vestibular reflex neurons is complementary to that of excitatory neurons.

the inhibition of tadpole superior oblique motoneneurons during vestibular stimulation is GABA-mediated and that the pharmacological profile correlates with rhombomer-specific origins and segmental abundance of vestibulo-oculor projection neurons.

the superior oblique motonuclei of anurans are reciprocally innervated by GABAergic and glutamatergic vestibular neurons and that this reciprocal innervation is mediated by two functionally distinct sets of GABAergic vestibular neurons, one of which is glycinergic.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the functional organization of brainstem pathways that mediate the vestibular excitation of eye muscles and the vestibular inhibition of their antagonists.
the identification and functional analysis of the neural substrates of vestibular reflexes.
the functional organization of the vestibulo-ocular reflex in anuran amphibians.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the superior oblique motonuclei receive an excitatory and an inhibitory input from the brainstem vestibular nuclei.
the pharmacology of vestibular inhibitions is not the same for all motoneurons, but rather depends on their specific location in the brainstem.
the superior oblique muscle is innervated by a vestibulo-ocular reflex pathway which is exclusively mediated via GABAergic neurons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the vestibulo-ocular reflex in anurans is mediated by a GABAergic inhibition of superior oblique and a glycinergic inhibition of lateral rectus motoneneurons.

the vestibular excitation of superior oblique and lateral rectus motneurons is mediated by the same type of excitatory neurons, whereas vestibular inhibition of these motoneurons is mediated by two distinct types of inhibitory neurons, one GABAergic and the other glycinergic.

the vestibular inhibition of superior oblique and lateral rectus motoneneurons is GABAergic and glycineric, respectively, in Xenopus tadpoles and that this pharmacology is likely conserved in all vertebrate species.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pharmacological profile of vestibulo-oculomotor neurons is determined by their rhombomere of origin and that it is highly conserved across vertebrate classes.
vestibular excitation of extraocular motones is not the sole determinant of VOR gain.

the GABAergic and glycineergic inhibitory components of vestibular inputs to motoneurons are reciprocally organized, and that this organization is based on rhombomere specific origins of vestibular projection neurons.
